title: Apply for a firearms licence (individual)
summary: This page provides information on how to apply for a NSW firearms licence as an individual.
intro:
When you apply for a NSW firearms licence you must provide evidence of your genuine reason for the possession and use of firearms.

The protection of yourself or another person is not considered a genuine reason.

You can have more than one genuine reason on your firearms licence.

Firearms licences are issued for 2 or 5 years with the exception of a:
who_can_apply: Be at least 18 years of age.
Be a fit and proper person to have access to firearms.
Have successfully completed a firearms training and safety course applicable to the type of firearm licence you are applying for.
Be able to provide evidence to justify your genuine reason for possessing or using a firearm.
what_you_need: Documentation to support each genuine reason/category.
A current credit card (Visa or Mastercard) for payment.
A copy of an eligible pensioner card (if applying for a Category A, B, or H licence).
Documentation required if applying for a licence over and above a Category A licence.
Documentation required if applying for a Category H firearm licence with the genuine reason of business or employment as an armed security guard.

how_to_steps.text: You will be taken to the NSW Police Force Community Self Service Portal.
Check that you have all the documentation required.
Follow the prompts to complete your application.

more_info.text: If you have any questions relating to firearms licences, please call the Firearms Registry customer service line on 1300 362 562 between 9am and 4pm Monday to Friday (excluding public holidays).

faqs.q: What is required to apply for a firearms licence?
faqs.a: Applicants must be at least 18 years old, be a fit and proper person, have completed a relevant firearms training and safety course, and provide evidence of a genuine reason for possession or use.

faqs.q: How long are firearms licences valid for?
faqs.a: Firearms licences are typically issued for 2 or 5 years.

faqs.q: What is considered a genuine reason for owning a firearm?
faqs.a: Applicants must provide evidence of a genuine reason for possession or use, but the protection of yourself or another person is not considered a genuine reason.
